questions.question: What is the first rule of ARIA, and why?
questions.answer: Do not use ARIA if a native HTML element already provides the semantics. Native elements expose role, state, and keyboard behavior automatically; ARIA only changes the accessibility tree and adds no behavior.

questions.question: What are the rules for alt text?
questions.answer: Describe the purpose or information of the image. Use alt="" for decorative images, describe the action for functional images in links/buttons, and repeat text for text-in-image. Never use filenames.

questions.question: How do aria-label, aria-labelledby, and aria-describedby differ?
questions.answer: aria-label sets the accessible name directly. aria-labelledby references one or more element ids to build the name (and wins over aria-label). aria-describedby adds supplemental description without replacing the name.

questions.question: Why is aria-hidden dangerous on focusable elements?
questions.answer: It removes the element from the accessibility tree but not from keyboard focus, creating a ghost control that keyboard users can reach but screen readers cannot announce. Remove it from the DOM or add tabindex=-1.

questions.question: Write an accessible icon button that closes a dialog.
Associate a password field with helper text and an error message.
questions.answer:
Use at least 8 characters.

Password is too short.

questions.question:
Why is
Save
incomplete?
questions.answer: A div is not focusable or keyboard-operable by default. It needs tabindex=0, Enter/Space handlers, and visible focus styles. Using a real button gives all of that for free.

questions.question: What contrast and zoom requirements does WCAG set for text?
questions.answer: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text under AA, with visible focus indicators, and content must remain usable at 200% zoom without blocked pinch-zoom.
